standard.title: Manipulate elements and use compositional devices
standard.description: manipulate elements of music and use compositional devices to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning when composing and practising music for performance, and notate, document and/or record the music they compose
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can manipulate elements of music to communicate ideas and practise for performance, using notation to document work (AC9AMU4C01). They can use multiple documentation formats and work collaboratively on accompaniments. They have not yet applied formal compositional devices (form, contrast, repetition) to structure compositions, or composed for specific instruments within technical constraints.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students manipulate elements of music and apply compositional devices to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, notating, documenting or recording the work in a format that supports rehearsal and performance.

nodes.label: What compositional devices are
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe at least two compositional devices (e.g. repetition, contrast, a given form such as verse/chorus or binary) and recognise them when listening.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two compositional devices in a piece of music; describe what each device does to the music's structure or effect.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe compositional devices in diverse musical examples — repetition, contrast, verse/chorus form, binary, ternary, ostinato; explain how each device structures the music and serves the communicative purpose.
wider: Compare two pieces in different forms (e.g. verse/chorus vs binary) and describe how the structural difference affects the listener's experience

Listen to examples of the same compositional device used in different genres or cultural contexts — how does repetition function differently in a pop song vs a West African drum pattern vs a Bach invention?
nodes.hinge_reason: Compositional devices are the new conceptual demand of this standard. Students who can manipulate elements but have no understanding of compositional devices as structural tools cannot 'use' them — they can only accidentally reproduce them. Without this conceptual foundation, the higher-order compositional work in AC9AMU8C01/C02 and AC9AMU10C01/C02 is inaccessible.

response_modes.reason: Introduce compositional devices through analysis before application. Listen to a verse/chorus song and identify the structural pattern before asking students to compose in that form. 'What repeats? What contrasts? What is the effect of that repetition/contrast?' Analysis first, composition second.

success_criteria: Can name at least two compositional devices and describe what each does
Can identify at least two compositional devices when listening to a musical example

nodes.label: Using compositional devices to structure a composition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use at least one compositional device to structure a composition with a clear communicative intention.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose a piece using at least one compositional device (e.g. verse/chorus form or deliberate repetition); state the communicative intention and explain how the device serves it.
nodes.typical_width: Compose pieces using multiple compositional devices across different contexts — structuring a song with verse/chorus, using repetition and contrast to shape a melody, composing in binary or ternary form; connect each structural decision to the communicative or expressive intention; compose in response to a theme, image or cross-curricular question.
wider: Work collaboratively to compose a song for a cross-curricular presentation — use both element manipulation and compositional devices, and explain why each choice serves the communication task
Arrange or re-imagine a known work by applying a different compositional device — compose new lyrics and restructure the form, then compare the original and re-imagined versions

response_modes.reason: Compositional device application is richer across multiple purposes and contexts. Composing for different reasons (a cross-curricular song, a song with personal meaning, a soundscape for a ceremony) requires different device choices — context breadth develops flexible structural thinking.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Composition in response to diverse prompts (images, themes, cross-curricular questions, cultural purposes) is genuinely rich — each new context requires students to think freshly about which devices and manipulations serve that specific communicative purpose.
success_criteria: Composes a piece using at least one identified compositional device
Can explain how the device serves the stated communicative intention

nodes.label: Composing within technical constraints
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compose a melody or instrumental part within a defined technical constraint (e.g. a limited pitch range, specific instruments) and use digital tools to complete the work.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose a melody or part for a specific instrument within a stated constraint (e.g. using only the notes they can play); use at least one digital tool to supplement or complete the work.
nodes.typical_width: Compose for specific instruments within technical constraints — using a pitch range matching their instrumental skill level; combining live performance with digital tools (loops, notation software); composing voices and instruments parts that are within the players' technical capability.
wider: Combine loops constructed from melodic or rhythmic patterns with live performance — design the loop and live components so they complement each other
Use notation software to create a score for voice and instruments — perform from the score and evaluate whether the notation accurately captures the intended performance

response_modes.reason: Composing within constraints integrates element manipulation, compositional devices and technical knowledge of instruments. The teaching investment is in making constraint-based composition a creative discipline rather than a limitation: 'Within these five notes, what can you create?'

success_criteria: Composes a melody or part that respects a stated technical constraint
Documents the composition in a format (notation or recording) that supports rehearsal

nodes.label: Notating, documenting and recording compositions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can notate, document or record a composition in a format appropriate to the type of music and suitable for use in rehearsal and performance.
nodes.minimum_width: Document a composition using a format matched to the music type (e.g. lead-sheet for a song, graphic/staff notation or recording for an instrumental piece) with sufficient detail to reconstruct it in rehearsal.
nodes.typical_width: Use a combination of notation formats, audio recording and digital tools to document compositions; ensure documentation captures element manipulation decisions and structural devices; use documentation in rehearsal to maintain fidelity to compositional intent.
wider: Create a combined graphic and staff notation document for a piece — use graphic notation for soundscape sections and staff notation for melodic sections; evaluate which format works better for each section
Use digital loop and notation tools to create a multi-track recorded and notated score — compare the information captured by each format

response_modes.reason: Y5-6 students benefit from consolidating and extending their documentation repertoire. Different composition types require different documentation approaches — the goal is fluent selection of appropriate tools, not mastery of one format.

success_criteria: Documents a composition in a format matched to its type
Documentation is detailed enough to guide a rehearsal without relying entirely on memory
